newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Alpha Finance posts 27pct rise in 96 pretax.
newsitem.headline: Greek Alpha Finance posts 27pct rise in 96 pretax.

text.p: Greece's Alpha Finance posted an increase of 27 percent in pretax profits to 3.144 billion drachmas in 1996 against 2.478 billion in 1995, its chairman Panayis Vourloumis told the annual shareholders' meeting on Thursday.
"Alpha Finance did better in 1996 than in the previous year in its main activities and improved its internal organisation," said Vourloumis.
Alpha Finance is the investment arm of the Alpha Credit Bank group.

Alpha Finance's total revenues increased by 23.6 percent to 4.53 billion drachmas in 1996 and its equity capital rose to 7.68 billion drachmas in 1996 from 3.669 billion in 1995 as the result of reinvesting part of 1996 profits, said Vourloumis.
"After eight years of valuable experience we feel strong enough to cross our borders into neighbouring countries," he said. "We have already assumed works in Romania, Bulgaria, Armenia and Georgia."
Alpha Finance is now controlling the Bucharest Investment Group in Romania which offers advisory services to business and brokerage services.
"We plan to help the Bucharest Investment Group with capital and executives," he said.
Alpha Finance is the only Greek company licensed by the SEC to provide investment advice to U.S. organisations, Vourloumis added.

The firm works closely with well known international investment firms such as Barclays de Zoette Wedd, Rotchild & Sons, Finnish Telecon to advise telecom OTE, state Public Gas Corporation (DEPA) on various projects, he said.

Alpha Finance also has a 21 percent stake in the Alpha mutual fund management company, 46.6 percent in Alpha Ventures and 16.1 percent in Romanian Banca Bucuresti which has a network of nine branches, said Vourloumis.
"Alpha Finance will participate in its (Banca Bucaresti) share capital increase planned for 1997," he added.
Alpha Credit Bank owns 40 percent of Banca Bucaresti and EBRD 20 percent. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
